title: Roadmap sync scratchpad — Product / Eng / Applied ML (Mar 2026)
content:
Purpose / context:
- Prep notes for cross-functional roadmap alignment sync (Product + Eng + Applied ML). Quick personal scratchpad — not polished.
- Goal: clarify dependencies and tradeoffs for H1 features that touch model routing, quantization recommendations, and rollout safety nets.

Participants to ping (confirm): Ravi (eng infra), Maya (applied ML), Ethan (product design), Samir (SRE?), Claire (security) — ask Claire if we should include compliance brief.

High-level goals for this sync:
1) Align on scope and go/no-go criteria for the "adaptive routing" work that will let us route to quantized variants under load.
2) Agree an experiments plan (A/B / canary) and basic telemetry required to detect quality regressions early.
3) Identify critical infra / kernel changes that must land before Dedicated beta.
4) Lock primary owners and 30/60/90 day milestones.

Top talking points (talking order idea):
- 0–5m: quick status / sprint context (what shipped last week that affects this: KV cache parity, batcher tweaks).
- 5–20m: Product lays out roadmap changes + use-cases (Ethan) — expected latency/cost targets for customers.
- 20–40m: Applied ML shows quality delta matrix between float/FP16/4-bit quantized on our eval sets (Maya) + open concerns.
- 40–55m: Eng: runtime/serving constraints; kernel scheduling + availability windows (Ravi).
- 55–65m: Agreement on rollout strategy + canary config + telemetry (all).
- 65–75m: Action items, owners, deadlines, parking lot.

Notes to self (rough, incomplete):
- Product wants to advertise "quant-aware routing" as a feature in marketing. Must ensure we have robust fallback to higher-precision models when quality drops.
- Key metric for rollout = customers seeing >2x token-cost reduction without >5% decline in top-level eval score (whatever that means for customer). Need definition: relative BLEU? For multi-turn chat need response-quality SLO — propose using a composite metric: eval-weighted perplexity + human rating sample.
- Telemetry: token_cost_per_request, mean_generation_latency_95, eval_score_delta_daily, routing_fallback_rate. Need SLO thresholds in doc.

Applied ML bulletin (Maya) — summary I expect from her:
- Small subset (RW-llm-13b) quant -> 4-bit (q4_k_m) shows 3–4% degradation on our standard eval set but negligible on reranking tasks.
- Degradation concentrated on rare token sequences and multi-step reasoning.
- Proposed mitigations: mixed-precision selective layers; post-filtering rerank; confidence-based fallback on low-likelihood tokens.
- Open question: do we want to implement on-the-fly selective dequantization (hot-path) or keep a separate higher-precision replica? Cost trade-offs.

Engineering constraints (Ravi) — items to surface before sync:
- Kernel changes for q4 handling not yet merged: PR#987 is blocking (linked). Need perf tests on p4d equivalence and a regression run on p3/p4.
- Router needs to be able to mark a model variant as "degraded" with a TTL; current system supports by-model health but not per-variant scoring.
- Autoscaler must incorporate cost vs latency objective; currently autoscaler tunes for throughput only. Likely 2–3 weeks to prototype.

Decision points I want to push for in meeting (priority order):
- Agree to a conservative rollout: enable quantized routing only for beta orgs, with an explicit fallback threshold and daily quality gate.
- Require an "experiment dashboard" before any external announcement. The dashboard must show both cost and quality trade-offs and provide drill-down on falldown reasons.
- Approve timeboxed engineering spike (2w) to add variant-level health / routing metrics.

Draft rollout proposal (my suggested phrasing):
Phase 0: internal gated experiments on staging with synthetic traffic and our eval suites (Maya + Eng infra).
Phase 1: invite-only Dedicated customers (opt-in) with telemetry enabled; 1-week canary windows; automatic rollback if eval_score_delta_daily > 4% or fallback_rate > 1%.
Phase 2: general availability with conservative default routing policy (prefer high-precision for multi-turn long context).

KPIs to track (initial):
- Cost per 1k tokens (median + 95th).
- Latency p95 and p99.
- Eval score delta (daily rolling) vs baseline.
- Fallback rate (requests switched to high-precision).
- Customer-reported quality incidents (CS triage).

Risks / mitigation (brain-dump):
- False negatives in quality detection -> could cause silent degradation. Mitigate: random human sampling with lightweight label tool; more conservative thresholds.
- Kernel regressions causing latency spikes -> require perf gates + synthetic perf suite.
- Autoscaler oscillation if cost objective added -> smoothing window + panic button to disable cost-aware routing.

Action items (concrete) — assign now if possible:
- Maya: finalize quantization quality matrix and upload a short summary doc + recommended thresholds. Due: 2026-03-19. (linked_artifacts: will add)
- Ravi: scope variant-health work + PR timeline; rough ETA for spike + QA. Due: 2026-03-17.
- Ethan: draft the customer-facing feature brief + suggested messaging for beta. Due: 2026-03-20.
- Avery (me): build experiment dashboard mock (Grafana panels) and pull initial queries for cost/quality. Due: 2026-03-18.
- Claire: quick compliance check re: telemetry collection & PII risk (opt-in vs opt-out). Due: 2026-03-22.

Questions to ask in the meeting (short list):
- Maya: which eval signals most robust to quantization? Can we get per-example confidence to trigger fallback?
- Ravi: how painful is adding variant-level health metadata? Any backward-compat issues with older routing clients?
- SRE: acceptable rollback time objective if quality gate fails? How quickly can we scale up high-precision replicas?
- Product: what level of marketing claim is safe? "Cost-aware routing" vs "quant-aware routing" subtlety — legal?

Parking lot (things to file elsewhere):
- Long-term: integrate quality-aware RL loop to continuously retrain quantization knobs.
- Infra: standardize benchmark harness across cloud regions (us-east-1 vs eu-west-1) — we've seen perf shifts.

Meeting logistics (my plan):
- 75 min slot, record, capture action items in Linear, follow up thread in #roadmap-sync.
- Start with high-level ask then dig into constraints — keep engineering block to 20 min.
- I will draft meeting note template for scribe (Ravi?) so we collect the exact gating thresholds, who owns the rollback, and telemetry queries.

Scribe template (quick):
- Decisions made: 
- Open questions: 
- Action items (owner, due, ticket if any): 

Quick rough tickets I should create after meeting (TODO):
- LNR-xxx: spike: variant-level health metadata + routing TTL (owner: Ravi)
- LNR-yyy: experiment dashboard panels (owner: Avery)
- LNR-zzz: quantization quality matrix doc (owner: Maya)

Random notes / voice-of-customer snippets to bring up:
- "We expect GA customers to see stable 30% cost wins for embeddings/call routing if quant works consistently." — check with growth to validate claim.
- Example customer: AdServeCo (placeholder) needs <50ms p95 for short responses — ensure quant path doesn't push over.

End-of-scratchpad reminders to self:
- Keep doc status = draft until we have dashboard + Maya sign-off.
- After meeting: convert action items to Linear with owners + link back here.
- Follow-up: schedule 30-min check-in 1 week after initial rollout to review metrics.

--
Personal note: keep tone pragmatic in meeting. My priority is risk reduction and measurable gates rather than shipping a headline feature too early.

[END OF SCRATCHPAD]
